title: Extreme flooding
description: The 1-in-100-year storm tide with 0.8 m of sea level rise by 2100 (2.40 m AHD), the basis of Melbourne Water's flood protection level for Southbank buildings, with heavy rain. Typical water on flooded footpaths is above the hip. A static estimate, not a hydraulic model: no flow or velocity.
sources: Level: typical (median) depth on flooded footpaths above the hip; body landmarks after Drillis & Contini (1966), as used to grade flood depth by Feng, Brenner & Sester (2020).

Mechanisms: Melbourne Water, Southbank Precinct Local Floodplain Development Plan (2026): river flooding from storm tide and river flows; local stormwater flooding, shallow but widespread, made worse when high tailwater stops the drains discharging.
Storm tide levels for Port Phillip Bay: GHD for Melbourne Water (2017), Fishermans Bend Baseline Drainage Plan, Table 1: 5-year 1.10, 20-year 1.25, 100-year 1.60 m AHD; 100-year in 2100 2.40 m AHD.
Sea level rise allowance: Victoria Planning Provisions clause 13.01-2S, at least 0.8 m by 2100.

Drain backflow: City of Melbourne Municipal Emergency Management Plan, Flood and Storm Sub-plan (2025): a high tide reduces the drains' capacity to discharge and backflow surcharges around the drainage pits; rain over 20 mm/h for an hour or more is likely to cause flash flooding.
Stormwater ponding: closed depressions of the ground model, anywhere in the area.
Drain inlets: City of Melbourne open data, Stormwater Pits (CC BY 4.0), surface inlets only.
Ground: Geoscience Australia 5 m LiDAR digital elevation model (CC BY 4.0).
